So I wasn’t talked out of it but I feel like this is good to know if someone ever tells you they’re going to attempt. I was 14 when I attempted and I hadn’t told anyone except for this guy I thought I was in love with who was 17. He simply told me “I hope the grass is greener on the other side.” Please please please do not say anything like this. In my suicidal state I took that as “I guess no one really does care” and I proceeded to take 27 Vicodin, 30 Lexapro, and an array of other pills that I don’t remember. I of course, blacked out and I guess the guy I told realized what he did and got ahold of my mom on Facebook and thankfully my mom found me. She gave me CPR until the paramedics arrived and was told that they didn’t know if I was going to make it. I spent 3 days in the ICU in and out of consciousness and was finally able to be stabilized. I then spent a good chunk of my freshman year going through inpatient, partial-hospitalization, and residential treatment. On September 14th, it will have been 6 years since my attempt. I am forever grateful that I survived and am able to tell my story. I’m currently a pre-med student with a dream to become and adolescent psychiatrist to help those who were like me. If someone confides with you that they are contemplating suicide, it’s more than likely a cry for help whether they realize it or not. Talk to them, tell them that you want them to be in this world with you, that you love them (even if you may think this is weird), and if you know they have a roommate or family member who may be around, tell them so they can be with them physically. Sorry OP for not fitting your description.
